text:
maria: Heads up — Support got a report where a streaming response was truncated client-side, client retried, and the customer saw 2x token usage. Repro steps attached.
kevin: Ugh. Is this the case where the client closed the socket and retried, and we generated a new stream id? Or where we resumed the same session?
maria: Client closed, retried a new request. The server did a short-circuit truncation because KV eviction happened mid-stream. We emitted partial-event then resumed on retry.
li: Do we currently emit billing events on partial_stream_end? I thought we waited for final_stream_end before accounting.
kevin: We emit intermediate increments for streaming chunks for near-real-time billing so the console can show usage live. That was the intentional tradeoff.
josh: That's the crux — incremental accounting vs eventual reconciliation. If a retry reproduces the same prefixes, we might charge both increments unless dedupe logic runs later.
maria: I captured logs. Example (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-20T15:12:03Z] stream_chunk id=abc token_count=120 prefix_hash=0x7f emit=increment
[2026-02-20T15:12:04Z] kv_eviction model=redi seq=512
[2026-02-20T15:12:05Z] stream_partial_end id=abc reason=truncated
[2026-02-20T15:12:07Z] new_request id=def on_retry prompt=... (same prompt)
[2026-02-20T15:12:07Z] stream_chunk id=def token_count=140 emit=increment
[2026-02-20T15:12:09Z] stream_final_end id=def token_total=260
```
kevin: So the customer sees 120 + 140 = 260 tokens charged, which matches the final successful response. Where's the double charge? maria: In this case, the first partial was also persisted to billing because our short-lived incremental ledger checkpoint wasn't rolled back when the partial stream ended with truncation. The reconciliation job runs later but lagging and some analytics/alerts already counted the incremental charge into invoice preview.
li: Ah — invoice preview and quota enforcement read the incremental ledger immediately, but the reconciliation denorm/rollback only happens in a background pass. Race.
josh: We should separate two concerns: (1) near-real-time console usage (best-effort, can be adjusted) (2) actual invoiceable ledger (source of truth, consistent). Right now we mix them.
kevin: Options:
  - Stop emitting incremental billing events until stream_final_end (pros: correct; cons: console UX worse and we can't show live usage)
  - Emit increments but mark them provisional and don't surface to invoice/quotas until finalization/timeout
  - Keep as-is but make reconciliation deterministic and faster (reduce windows where preview disagrees)
maria: I like provisional markers. Also need to handle tool calls specially. If a streaming response triggers a toolcall mid-stream and that toolcall does external API calls (and consumes tokens), and the client retries the whole request, we must avoid charging both the tool invocation and the retried tool invocation twice if the tool itself is idempotent — but we can't rely on that.
li: For toolcalls we already pass an idempotency_key when platform invokes internal tools, but external connectors may not be idempotent.
kevin: Proposal: bill toolcall execution immediately (external cost), but in the customer ledger mark them as "tool-exec:provisional" until final_stream_end. On final success mark "confirmed". If the retry causes a duplicate confirmed exec, we dedupe by toolcall-idempotency if available; otherwise do a best-effort reconciliation and issue a credit if double-billed.
josh: Credits are messy and break SLAs. Can we require connector authors to be idempotent? Not realistic short-term.
li: Also quotas: if we provisionally charge a quota bucket on incremental emits, a retry could make it appear exceeded. For UX we should surface "pending usage" vs "billed usage" in console and not block in-flight requests on provisional increments.
maria: Another vector: truncation vs server-side abort. If we truncate due to max_tokens, that's a client-visible outcome and should be billed for produced tokens. But if we abort because of transient internal error and the client retries, we should avoid double billing. Need to distinguish reasons.
kevin: Agreed. We should classify finalization reasons: success, client_cancel, server_error, truncated_by_policy. Only "success" and "truncated_by_policy" confirm provisional increments. "server_error" or socket-level disconnects should trigger rollback.
ops-bot: @channel Note: there's an existing RFC draft at <internal/rfcs#stream-billing-2026> that touches part of this. It currently recommends provisional increments with a 5s stabilization window.
maria: 5s is too short for some retries (mobile flaky nets). I'd prefer a 30s window with exponential backoff after repeated retries, but that increases exposure for provisional counts.
kevin: Implementation plan I'm comfortable with:
  1) Mark streaming increments as provisional (flag: provisional=true).
  2) Publish these to console as "pending usage" only.
  3) Do not consume quota or trigger invoice-preview until finalization OR until provisional timeout (default 30s) expires and status==success/truncated_by_policy.
  4) If finalization reason==server_error or client_cancel -> rollback provisional increments immediately (emit compensation event to ledger).
  5) For toolcalls: attach toolcall_id to incremental events; if same toolcall_id confirmed twice, reconcile by dedupe using idempotency keys; if not dedupeable, mark credit-required and create a ticket pipeline to credit.
li: We'll need extra telemetry: provisional_count, provisional_to_confirm_ratio, compensation_rate, avg-finalization-latency. I'll add a dashboard and alerts if compensation_rate > 0.5% for 10m.
josh: API changes: add status in streaming proto (pending|confirmed|rolled_back) and a finalization/reason envelope. Console: show pending vs billed in UI and add tooltip explaining provisional semantics.
maria: Docs/SDK: we should surface an event or callback clients can opt into (stream_finalized(reason)) so they can avoid retrying if reason==truncated_by_policy.
kevin: Edge-case: long-running toolcalls that finish after finalization — e.g., stream_final_end occurs but background toolcall completes later and consumes tokens. We should treat toolcall tokens as independent lines in the ledger and only confirm once toolcall returns. Means finalization can't confirm toolcall tokens until both stream and toolcall are done.
josh: Put that in RFC.
li: I'll prototype telemetry and a reconciler job to run every 10s instead of 1m. If we see instability we'll back off.
kevin: I'll open a PR for ledger flags + reconciler and a small console change to hide provisional from quota enforcement. Link it here when ready.
maria: Thanks. Assigning action items: kevin -> PR, li -> metrics + dashboard, josh -> RFC update, maria -> support doc explaining when you'll see pending vs billed. We'll also notify Finance about provisional preview mismatch.
billing-bot: Created ticket FIN-834 for reconciliation policy review.
maria: Cool. If anyone objects to the heuristics above speak up today, otherwise we'll ship a beta flag to Dedicated customers next week. :thumbsup:
